context.objective: Document how we carry out Cash Reconciliation & Working Capital Reporting, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text:
It starts when cash activity shows up in the bank portal, when the monthly bank reconciliation turns up activity, or when a planned capital event needs a liquidity analysis. Here is the whole thing end to end:
1. Cash-composition preparer: carry the Cash Composition workbook into the new period, create the new monthly tab, carry forward the beginning balance and confirm it matches the prior ending balance and the actual bank balance including sweep accounts.
2. Cash-composition preparer: review new bank activity and anything found in the monthly bank reconciliation, validate account, entity, date, amount and direction, and make sure nothing is recorded twice.
3. Cash-composition preparer: enter one row per movement in the Cash Analysis tab with date, description, amount, category and a reference to support.
4. Cash-composition preparer: classify each movement as a source (capital call, LOC draw, proceeds), a use (investment, management fee, expense, LOC repayment, distribution) or due to or from affiliates. If a movement is unclear or mixed-purpose, it goes to the fund team or client for clarification and stays an open exception until they answer; we do not guess.
5. Cash-composition preparer: add each movement to the life-to-date sources and uses on the Cash Composition tab, each amount linked to its transaction.
6. Cash-composition preparer: total the categories and compare to the bank balance including sweep accounts. If they do not match, investigate missing items, duplicates, broken formulas and misclassifications and repeat until they match; any difference that remains is escalated and the report is not relied on. If they match, continue.
7. Cash-composition preparer: log known expected outflows from client notices or approved internal commitments, kept separate from cash already in the GL, and update or close them when the cash moves.
8. Cash-composition preparer with the fund or capital-activity team: build the pre, during and post event view - starting cash by category, the event inflows and outflows, ending cash by category. If pending outflows exceed available cash, flag the shortfall and send it to the client or fund team for the capital-event or payment decision; proceed only after that is done.
9. Cash-composition preparer: when applicable, record who paid and when from portal and bank details and match investor receipt totals to the Cash Composition amount.
10. Cash-composition preparer and quarterly reviewer: copy the current report into the quarterly supporting files, do the detailed quarterly review, list corrections, and escalate any difference between the quarterly copy and the Treasury-folder copy.
11. Fund or capital-activity team: tell the decision-makers the available cash, amounts set aside, pending obligations and projected ending balance, say whether a capital call, hold or other action is needed, and keep the reconciliation, event view, source records and exceptions with the period supporting files. That is the end.
Which role is accountable for the overall cash reconciliation and working-capital reporting result?

I do not know - the overall process owner and the internal approver have not been confirmed yet. What I can say is that the client or fund has to authorize the later liquidity or capital-event decision, but exactly where that approval happens is not confirmed either.
What does the quarterly reviewer check in the detailed review?

The category has to be based on identifiable activity in the transaction records. Sources are cash coming in - capital calls, LOC draws, proceeds received. Uses are cash going out - investments, management fees, organizational and other expenses, LOC repayments, distributions. Due to or from affiliates is amounts owed between the fund and related entities and is kept as its own category. A workbook formula, a prior report or someone's memory is not a rule by itself. Which entity, transaction and repayment details are required for affiliate items is not confirmed yet.
In the detailed quarterly review, what does the reviewer compare or check?

They give us the source records and transaction details for that movement, and we keep the supporting documents or correspondence as the record. Beyond that I do not know exactly what they look at on their side. Until we have it, the item stays an open exception and that item does not move forward.
How often does the cash reconciliation work normally occur?

The cash-composition preparer carries the Cash Composition workbook into a new period, creates a monthly tab, carries forward the beginning balance, and confirms it matches the prior ending balance and actual bank balance including sweep accounts.
